story_title: NVIDIA NVLink Fusion Expands With NVHBM Custom High-Bandwidth Memory
why_this_story: NVIDIA is altering standard chip architecture by moving the memory controller off the compute die into a 3D HBM stack, freeing up to 25% compute die area for trillion-parameter AI workloads.
viral_angle: NVIDIA solved the AI memory bottleneck by re-engineering chip layout—and surprisingly, AWS is integrating it directly into its next-gen Trainium chips.
story_sentence: Everyone thinks AI chips just need faster transistors, but NVIDIA is moving the memory controller into 3D stacks to free up 25% compute space.

caption:
NVIDIA just made a major change to how AI hardware is built.

As AI models reach trillion-parameter scales, standard HBM architecture runs into a physical bottleneck: memory controllers on the main XPU die take up precious silicon area.

NVIDIA's new NVHBM technology moves the memory controller directly into the 3D HBM stack. 

The technical gains according to NVIDIA:
• Up to 30% greater memory bandwidth
• Up to 15% lower memory power consumption
• Frees up to 25% compute area on the main die

In a surprising move, Amazon’s Annapurna Labs is the first official partner, planning to support NVLink Fusion with its next-generation Trainium4 chips.
